demo_cases.title: NSCLC Adjuvant Therapy — Low-Resource Clinic
demo_cases.scenario: 68-year-old former smoker presenting with fatigue and persistent cough. Limited diagnostic infrastructure.

patient_intake.clinical_history: 40 pack-year smoking history, quit 5 years ago. Presenting with 6-week progressive cough and constitutional symptoms. No prior cancer history.
patient_intake.clinician_question: Patient has completed primary surgical resection (left lower lobe wedge, margins negative). No adjuvant chemotherapy yet offered. What is the evidence-based recommendation for adjuvant therapy given limited biomarker testing capability?

imaging_summary.primary_tumor: 3.2 cm left lower lobe mass, heterogeneous enhancement, irregular borders
imaging_summary.lymph_nodes: 1 cm left hilar lymph node (involved), no other suspicious nodes
imaging_summary.notes: Post-surgical changes consistent with wedge resection. No obvious recurrence.

demo_cases.voice_note_transcript: Patient is otherwise fit, good performance status. Asking about chemotherapy. Wife is very concerned about recurrence risk. Patient prefers oral medication if available. Also asking whether we should wait for more biomarker testing before deciding on treatment.

key_findings: Stage IIIA NSCLC post-resection with nodal involvement (N1)
KRAS G12C mutation identified (targetable with sotorasib/adagrasib)
PD-L1 18% (low expression, chemotherapy likely preferred over single-agent ICI)
Adjuvant chemotherapy indicated per NCCN guidelines (Level 1 evidence)
KRAS G12C targeted therapy could be considered if available
recommendations: Consider sequential KRAS G12C inhibitor (sotorasib) if available in local setting
Follow-up biomarker testing (MSI-H, TMB) recommended to guide future surveillance/therapy
Clinical trial enrollment for KRAS-mutant NSCLC if accessible
red_flags: PD-L1 18% does not support single-agent checkpoint inhibition
Limited biomarker panel — missing MSI/TMB could impact prognosis
expected_ai_output_summary.next_steps: Initiate adjuvant chemotherapy; refer to oncology for KRAS-targeted therapy discussion if available

demo_cases.title: HER2+ Breast Cancer — Neoadjuvant Planning
demo_cases.scenario: 52-year-old post-menopausal woman with locally advanced HER2-positive breast cancer. Regional hospital with advanced molecular testing.

patient_intake.known_diagnosis: Invasive ductal carcinoma, HER2-positive, Stage IIIA
patient_intake.clinical_history: Presented with 2.1 cm palpable mass in right upper quadrant. No prior cancer history. Negative for BRCA1/2. Post-menopausal, no systemic therapy yet.
patient_intake.clinician_question: Recently diagnosed with HER2+ invasive ductal carcinoma. Patient is concerned about recurrence risk and asking specifically about trastuzumab-based neoadjuvant therapy. Would this be appropriate? What is the evidence-based approach for this stage/subtype?

pathology_summary.histology: Invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), no special type

imaging_summary.primary_tumor: 2.1 cm heterogeneous enhancing mass in right upper quadrant, spiculated margins
imaging_summary.lymph_nodes: 1 cm right axillary node (likely involved), no supraclavicular involvement
imaging_summary.notes: Clip placed in tumor for post-treatment identification. No skin involvement.

demo_cases.voice_note_transcript: Patient is very motivated and wants most aggressive treatment available. Asking if trastuzumab will definitely prevent recurrence. Concerned about side effects. Partner is supportive. Patient is otherwise healthy, good cardiac function.

key_findings: HER2+ (IHC 3+, FISH confirmed) invasive ductal carcinoma
Hormone receptor positive (ER/PR+), suggesting luminal HER2 subtype
Regional nodal involvement (N1) — neoadjuvant therapy strongly indicated
recommendations: Trastuzumab-based neoadjuvant therapy is standard-of-care (strong Level 1 evidence)
Consider dual HER2 targeting (trastuzumab + pertuzumab per CLEOPATRA era data)
Add taxane chemotherapy (docetaxel preferred over paclitaxel for this setting)
Adjuvant endocrine therapy (tamoxifen or AI) post-surgery + continued trastuzumab
Consider de-escalation if pathologic complete response (pCR) achieved
red_flags: Grade 3 tumor with high Ki67 — aggressive biology
Nodal involvement increases recurrence risk if not adequately treated
Cardiac function must be monitored throughout trastuzumab therapy (baseline echo/MUGA recommended)
expected_ai_output_summary.next_steps: Baseline cardiac assessment; initiate taxane + trastuzumab + pertuzumab neoadjuvant regimen; surgical planning after response assessment

demo_cases.title: MSI-High CRC — Adjuvant vs. Surveillance Strategy
demo_cases.scenario: 61-year-old male with stage IIA microsatellite instability-high colorectal cancer post-resection. Resource-limited setting, considering surveillance vs. adjuvant therapy.

patient_intake.known_diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma of descending colon, MSI-H, Stage IIA
patient_intake.clinical_history: Presented with iron-deficiency anemia and hematochezia. Colonoscopy found 3 cm mass. Completed partial colectomy (D2 lymphadenectomy). No pre-treatment chemotherapy. Family history significant for Lynch syndrome screening (1 affected relative, not confirmed).
patient_intake.clinician_question: Post-resection imaging and labs normal. Pathology confirms MSI-H status. Patient is asking: Do I need adjuvant chemotherapy or can we just watch and wait? Resources are limited in our clinic. What is the evidence-based guidance for MSI-H Stage IIA?

imaging_summary.primary_tumor: Post-surgical changes, no residual mass visualized
imaging_summary.lymph_nodes: No suspicious lymph nodes identified (largest <1 cm)
imaging_summary.notes: Stapled anastomosis in place, no leak. CEA normal.

demo_cases.voice_note_transcript: Patient prefers surveillance if acceptable from oncology perspective — he has significant work responsibilities and worries about chemotherapy toxicity. Wife advocates for 'whatever is best.' No prior chemotherapy. Good performance status. Concerned about Lynch syndrome implications for screening of family members.

key_findings: MSI-H (dMMR confirmed) Stage IIA colon cancer — favorable prognosis
No lymph node involvement (N0) — lower recurrence risk
MSI-H is independent positive prognostic factor, associated with better outcomes
MSI-H status makes patient eligible for immunotherapy if recurrence occurs
Lynch syndrome screening indicated (family history positive, MLH1/PMS2 loss pattern suggests germline)
recommendations: Stage IIA MSI-H: Adjuvant chemotherapy may be deferred in selected cases (NCCN Category 2B)
Surveillance is reasonable option if patient well-informed about recurrence risk (~10-15%)
If chemotherapy preferred: 5-FU or FOLFOX reasonable, but benefit modest in MSI-H
Immunotherapy (checkpoint inhibition) NOT recommended adjuvantly, but important if recurrence develops
Lynch syndrome germline testing strongly recommended — impacts patient and family screening
red_flags: T3N0 status (transmural invasion) does increase local recurrence risk slightly
Lynch syndrome family history — requires genetic counseling and family communication
If surveillance chosen, must emphasize compliance with surveillance colonoscopy/imaging
expected_ai_output_summary.next_steps: Discuss surveillance vs. adjuvant chemotherapy with patient preferences; order germline Lynch testing; arrange genetic counseling; establish follow-up schedule (imaging + colonoscopy per NCCN)
